text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a regression on PP 1F1B after the new kernel selector landed (commit 3f9b2c4). End-to-end p95 latency up ~12% on 8xA100 runs, plus bigger PP bubbles/microbursting between steps. Attaching quick traces below.

sam: Which selector change specifically? link to PR?

maya: PR #8423 — selector now prefers `fused-mha-v2` for short seqs. Repro on internal perf-cluster with seq=1024, microbatch=4. Run id: run-2060-ppb.

profiler-bot: Automated profile for run-2060-ppb: compute_time=68%, all_reduce=18%, idle=14%. Noticeable spikes in all_reduce between microbatches.

jorge: I pulled the trace — all_reduce tails spike at the end of certain microbatches (ranks 0-3). Flamegraph shows imbalance: rank 2 waits ~22ms more than rank 5 frequently. Could be uneven KV cache eviction/restore cost.

li: Also see batching logs: batcher grouped sequences with high variance after the selector change (more short-seq preferred kernels), so microbatch compute duration variance increased. That hurts comm/compute overlap. Logs: ``microbatch_sizes=[4,4,2,6,4] pad_align=none``

ashley: Quick experiment idea: force the old kernel to confirm. Config override: ``kernel_preference: ["fused-mha-v1"]`` — if perf improves we know selector choice is causal.

maya: Ran that locally — latencies drop back to baseline (~-10% vs current), PP bubble amplitude reduces. But v1 had slightly different logits in some edge prompts (small quality diff).

sam: So v2 reduces compute per-step for short seqs on average but increases variance -> worse overlap. Two levers: adjust batching heuristics to reduce variance (pad_align, bucket by compute time) OR tune KV cache behavior to reduce eviction jitter.

jorge: On KV side, I noticed prefetch was turned off in that image (`kv_prefetch=false`). Enabling `kv_prefetch=true` reduced end-of-step all_reduce waiting by ~20% in a small run. Might be orthogonal but helpful.

li: I'll kick off a sweep: permutations = [kernel: v1,v2] x [pad_align: 0,8,16] x [kv_prefetch: true,false] x [microbatch=2,4,8]. ETA ~30m, I'll post the summary table.

profiler-bot: Sweep job 8120 started. Tracking metrics: p50/p95 latency, allreduce_mean, allreduce_imbalance, compute_variance, token_quality_regressions.

maya: If sweep confirms a combo that restores perf without quality loss, let's canary it on dedicated hosts. Also add a console metric for `allreduce_imbalance_ms` per-model so we can alert earlier.

sam: Agree — please add a lightweight tracepoint in runtime to emit per-step compute_time and allreduce_wait_time so we can correlate at scale.

ashley: Small config patch to try meanwhile (on canary only): ``batcher: {pad_align: 8, bucket_algo: "compute_estimate"}, runtime: {kv_prefetch: true}``

li: Sweep update (interim): early results show pad_align=8 + kv_prefetch=true + kernel=v2 reduces p95 by ~6% vs current and cuts allreduce_imbalance by ~30% while keeping token quality equal within eval thresholds. Full matrix finish in ~18m.

jorge: Nice — that suggests batching + kv prefetch recovers overlap losses introduced by kernel v2. If confirmed, we should encode a heuristic: when kernel selector picks v2, prefer pad_align=8 for microbatching profiles with high seq variance.

maya: Good plan — once full results in, I'll open a tracking ticket for rollout and AB test on a subset of clusters. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
